hero.title: Your business is like no other. Your software shouldn't be either.
hero.lead: We take the measure of your process before writing the first line of code. It's not a factory. It's tailoring.

idea.title: Off-the-shelf software almost fits. And almost fitting doesn't fit.
idea.p1: Every ready-made system was designed for the average of a market. Your process isn't the average. So you bend your operation to the system, build spreadsheets on the side, train people to work around what the tool can't do, and call that normal.
idea.p2: We go the other way. First we understand how your business really works, including the parts nobody ever documented. Then we build the piece around that.
idea.p3: It's close work, with only a few clients at a time. You can't take the measure of ten companies in the same month.

versus.eyebrow: Two ways of doing the same thing

steps.title: Measure
steps.body: We sit down with the people who run the process and watch how it happens today. That's diagnosis, not requirements gathering. A large part of the value is translating what you feel is wrong into something that can be built.

steps.title: Fit
steps.body: The software adapts to your process. If your operation has a step that no system on the market expects, it goes in exactly as it is. You don't twist yourself to fit another company's mold.

steps.title: Adjust
steps.body: The piece doesn't die at delivery. The business changes, the piece follows. We keep caring for it, fixing it and growing with you, because software nobody maintains ages fast.

case.name: AI-powered recruiting
case.title: A screening agent built around the way a recruiting firm works.
case.lead: The operation lived in spreadsheets and WhatsApp chats. Instead of taking the spreadsheet away from the end client, we built the agent around it. Recruiters keep working the way they always have, except now reading and outreach happen on their own.

steps.label: Step 01
steps.title: Job sync
steps.body: The end client updates the job spreadsheet in Excel online. From the dashboard, the recruiter triggers a read of the file. New openings are registered and the requirements of existing ones are updated.

steps.label: Step 02
steps.title: Campaign and outreach
steps.body: The recruiter picks a message template and sends the campaign to that opening's candidate pool. The conversation starts on its own, and whoever replies arrives already screened.

items.a: It depends on the size of the problem, and we won't guess. First we understand what needs to be built, then we talk numbers. No proposal goes out before the diagnosis.

It depends on what the measuring reveals. What we avoid is the year-long project that only shows results at the end. The idea is to get the first useful part into production quickly and grow from there.
The relationship continues. The piece is maintained and adjusted as the business changes. If you want a project that ends and disappears, we're probably not the right fit.

items.q: I already have a system running. Can we work together?
items.a: Yes, and it's common. A good part of the work is building the missing piece around what you already use, without forcing anyone to replace everything at once.

items.q: My process is a bit unusual. Is that a problem?
items.a: It's usually why you're here. A non-standard process is exactly what no off-the-shelf system accepts, and it's where a tailor-made piece is worth the most.

contact.title: Tell us the problem. We'll get back to you.
contact.lead: You don't need a ready scope or to know what you want built. Just describe what's holding you back today.
